name: Sgt. Weaver
summary: A sergeant in Larry's operations section, an ex-Marine, photographed at the flight-scheduling boards inside the radio van (VN-0014). He was an E5 at the time of the bathroom shooting at the headquarters company and was the sergeant who showed up while the drunk gunman still had the pistol out — a central witness to that incident. On 2026-09-12, at the van: "Weaver was a cool guy and hung out with me a lot." Larry thinks Weaver or Chapman took the night-time picture of him in the van (VN-0015).
researchNotes: Unusually well-anchored for an unresolved person: the 2026-08-09 vision survey independently read the VN-0014 name tape as beginning 'WE...' before Larry supplied 'Weaver' — testimony and photograph converge. If the bathroom-shooting court-martial record is found (unresolved #11), Weaver should appear in it as a witness. The shield-shaped pocket patch in VN-0014 is a re-scan target that could carry the unit designation; its lettering sits below the current scan's resolution. 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0014-c18415711, -vn-0015-c18415735): the van crewing Larry gives, "Day shift was probably 4 guys and night shift there was 1 guy", puts Weaver in a section of about five, which is small enough that a morning report listing one man should list the others.
